issues.title: Replace Bricolage Grotesque with Inter across index.html, landing.html and pricing.html
issues.body:
## Observable result

Every page of the Aurora site currently renders its body copy and headings in Bricolage Grotesque. A visitor loading `/index.html`, `/landing.html` or `/pricing.html` should instead see all text in Inter, a neutral, widely used UI sans-serif, with no page left on the old typeface.

## What to change

- In `index.html`, `landing.html` and `pricing.html`, replace the `fonts.googleapis.com` stylesheet link with one requesting Inter (`display=swap`).
- In the inline `<style>` block of each of those files, change `body{font-family:"Bricolage Grotesque",sans-serif;...}` so the primary family is `Inter` ahead of the existing `sans-serif` fallback.

## Assumptions

- Inter was chosen as the "more professional" typeface: it is the common neutral default for product and SaaS sites, has generous lowercase clarity at small sizes, and needs no design decisions beyond a family swap.
- "More professional" was read as a change of typeface only: the existing heading weight and every other type setting stay as they are.
- The font continues to load from Google Fonts over a `<link>` tag, matching how the current typeface is delivered, so no new hosting or build step is introduced.
- Layout, `margin`/`padding` and all page copy stay untouched; this is a typeface change only.

## Acceptance condition

Opening `index.html`, `landing.html` and `pricing.html` in a browser shows body text and the `Aurora` heading rendered in Inter on all three pages; no file still references `Bricolage Grotesque`, and if the Inter stylesheet fails to load the text falls back to the generic `sans-serif` family rather than an unstyled serif.
